question: Under what condition does the Java compiler supply an automatic default constructor for a class?

options.text: The compiler always generates a zero-argument default constructor for every class.
Only when the class explicitly declares at least one parameterless constructor.
Whenever all declared fields within the class possess primitive default values.
Only when the class body contains zero explicit constructor declarations.

explanation: The Java compiler synthesizes a default zero-argument constructor if and only if no explicit constructor declarations of any kind exist within the class body.

question: What parameters are accepted by the compiler-synthesized default constructor in Java?

options.text: It takes boolean flags specifying whether final fields should be reset.
It takes varargs Object parameters initializing all object fields.
It takes no arguments (zero formal parameters).
It takes one Object parameter representing the enclosing instance.

explanation: By definition in the Java specification, the default constructor generated by the compiler takes zero arguments and has an empty parameter list.

question: What is the access modifier of the synthesized default constructor for a protected member inner class?

options.text: Package-private access, because constructors cannot inherit member class modifiers.
Public access, because default constructors always receive public visibility.
Protected access, exactly matching the accessibility modifier of the member class.
Private access, preventing any subclass outside the package from invoking super().

explanation: The synthesized default constructor always has the same access modifier as its declaring class. For a protected member inner class, the default constructor has protected accessibility.

question: What is the relationship between an explicit no-arg constructor and the compiler-provided default constructor?

options.text: They are distinct: writing an explicit no-arg constructor prevents default constructor creation.
An explicit no-arg constructor is invalid unless the class extends a class with a default constructor.
Writing an explicit zero-argument constructor produces what Java technically defines as the default constructor.
The compiler combines user-written no-arg constructors with the synthesized default constructor.

explanation: A user-written no-argument constructor is an explicit constructor. Once any explicit constructor is written, the compiler does not generate a default constructor.
